agreement: Agrees with briefs/tower/bus-data/INVENTORY.json on the set of damaged lines (identical 26 line numbers), on every raw_byte_len, and on 24 of 26 damage_class values and 26 of 26 recoverable values. Two damage_class disagreements, both listed under disagreements: line 3 and line 2527.

default.notes: Two or more complete board rows written onto one physical line. Proven by splitting at the literal separator and parsing each part independently (evidence.recovery_proof). Separator is a single 0x6e byte ('n') between '}' and '{' — a newline that arrived with its backslash stripped. The first part is compact-serialized ("id":"..."), the trailing part is spaced-serialized ("id": "..."): two different serializers on one line. Repair is a pure split; no byte is lost.

1.writer: Not a board writer: captured stdout of a search/grep-style tool. No id/from/topic/cwd present.
1.notes: Not a board row. The literal 16-byte text `1 matches in 1F:` at the head of the file. First of a three-line block (lines 1-3) of captured tool stdout. No JSON object, no field is extractable, nothing to recover into a row — the line should be deleted, not repaired. No local tool in ~/agent-core/primitives or ~/.local/bin prints the string 'matches in' (rg, this session), so the producing tool is UNKNOWN.

2.writer: Not a board writer: captured stdout of a search/grep-style tool. No id/from/topic/cwd present.
2.notes: Not a board row. The literal 15-byte text `[file] 628 (1):` — second line of the same captured tool-stdout block as lines 1 and 3.

3.writer: Not a board writer: captured tool stdout quoting the fields of a spine-daemon row (id spine-fddfcbe6-..., ts 2026-07-24T09:18:30Z). The quoted row itself was written by whatever emits spine-* ids; the physical line was written by the capturing tool.
3.notes: Not a board row. Third line of the captured tool-stdout block: five leading spaces, then `0: "spine-fddfcbe6-...", "ts": "2026-07-24T09:18:30Z", "cwd` — a numbered excerpt of a board row printed by a tool. There is no opening brace anywhere on the line, and it stops mid-key at `"cwd`. Both defects are real; the primary class is non_json_text because the line never was a serialized row, and the truncation is secondary. Unrecoverable: the tail is gone and the head was never JSON.
3.disagreement: Prior classed line 3 as `truncated`. It is truncated, but it is first of all non-JSON: it opens with five spaces and `0: ` and contains no `{`, and it is the third line of the lines 1-3 stdout capture. Classing it `truncated` implies a serialized row got cut; classing it `non_json_text` says what the bytes are. recoverable=false either way.

553.notes: Single complete row, not a concatenation. Its body carries bare `"` characters (a $task-token quoted inline, `text "tower ask"`) which close the JSON string early — V8 reports `Expected ',' or '}' after property value` at byte 393. Recoverable and proven: escaping the bare quotes inside the trailing "body" value makes the row JSON.parse cleanly (evidence.recovery_proof). Agrees with prior: unescaped_body, recoverable.

2113.notes: Single complete row. The body quotes Rust source — `name.replace(\-\,_\)` — whose backslashes are not valid JSON escapes; V8 reports `Bad escaped character` at byte 1354. Recoverable and proven: escaping each stray backslash makes the row parse. Agrees with prior: invalid_escape, recoverable.

2527.notes: Two defects on one line. It is concatenated (one 0x6e separator; the trailing 326-byte spaced-serialized spine-daemon object parses as-is after the split), AND the leading 3400-byte compact worker object carries bare `"` characters in its body (`wait_for("c new")`, byte 774 of the line) so it does not parse even after the split. Recoverable and proven: split at '}n{', then escape the bare quotes in the leading object's body, and both halves JSON.parse.
2527.disagreement: Prior classed it plain `concatenated_objects`. Per this brief's rule — a concatenation is only classified once each split part parses — 2527 fails that test: part 0 needs an escape repair as well. Class recorded as `concatenated_objects+escape_bare_quotes_in_body` so a repair pass does not assume a split alone will fix it. recoverable=true in both inventories.

2507.notes: Three complete rows on one physical line (two separators, both a single 0x6e byte): two compact-serialized c003 worker rows followed by one spaced-serialized spine-daemon row. All three parse after the split. This is the only 3-object line in the set.
